summary: Sawyer County, WI steel tower, about 84 ft, subject of a January 1983 sealed-bid notice; listed as gone while an OSM tag says ruins; no site description found.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, about 84 feet (per 1983 notice)
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone; an OpenStreetMap point for the site is tagged abandoned and in ruins

events.note: A notice dated January 6, 1983 invited sealed bids for a fire tower at the Seeley site, which the notice described as steel and about 84 feet tall; the excerpt does not say what the bids were for

evidence.supports: DNR said the state would no longer use its 72 fire lookout towers
evidence.quote: they will no longer use the state’s 72 fire lookout towers

evidence.supports: Most of the towers were built in the 1930s
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were built in the 1930s

evidence.supports: Notice is dated January 6, 1983 and was quoted from The Capital Times
Sealed bids were to go to the DNR Park Falls office
evidence.quote: Sealed bids will be received by the State of Wisconsin, Department of Natural Resources at the Park Falls DNR Area Headquarter

evidence.supports: Location given as Section 6, T42N, R7W, Sawyer County
evidence.quote: Seeley Fire Tower - Sec 6, T42N, R7W, Sawyer Co.
Approximate height of the steel fire tower is 84 feet.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone, at 46.14777, -91.28392

sources.title: DNR Officials Will No Longer Use Fire Lookout Towers
Seeley, Forest Lookouts (quoting The Capital Times, January 6, 1983)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list says gone, while the OpenStreetMap point is tagged abandoned and in ruins, which suggests something may stand on the site. No photo or description was found to settle it, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The 84-foot height comes from the 1983 notice and is converted to 25.6 m here. The notice's section and township (Sec 6, T42N, R7W) were not checked against the OSM coordinates. The ruins tag is a volunteer map tag, not a site visit. The WPR statements are statewide, not specific to this tower. The WPR copy read is undated; its cache metadata gives 2015-12-17, which the story does not state.
